payload.statement_nl: For every integer n>1 and every real number t with 0 <= t < 1, if a = floor(n*t), then E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n).

result_payload.proof_nl:
Fix an integer n > 1 and a real number t with 0 <= t < 1. Let a = floor(n t). Then a <= n t < a + 1, so dividing by the positive number n gives

a / n <= t < (a + 1) / n.

Now fix any integer k with 1 <= k <= n. Since k > 0, multiplying the inequality a / n <= t by k preserves the order:

k a / n <= k t.

The floor function is nondecreasing on the real numbers, so

floor(k a / n) <= floor(k t).

Because k is positive, dividing by k preserves the inequality:

floor(k a / n) / k <= floor(k t) / k.

Summing this over k = 1, 2, ..., n yields

sum_{k=1}^n floor(k a / n) / k <= sum_{k=1}^n floor(k t) / k.

Also, since a is an integer, floor(n (a / n)) = floor(a) = a, and by definition floor(n t) = a. Therefore

E_n(t) = floor(n t) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k t) / k
       = a - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k t) / k
       <= a - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k a / n) / k
       = floor(n (a / n)) - sum_{k=1}^n floor(k a / n) / k
       = E_n(a / n).

This is exactly the desired inequality.
result_payload.proof_summary: On the interval determined by a = floor(nt), each term floor(kx) is monotone in x, so the sum increases from x = a/n to x = t while the leading term floor(nx) stays equal to a; hence E_n(t) <= E_n(a/n).

used_external_facts: Multiplication and division by a positive number preserve inequalities.
